blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights EigenROP, a novel anomaly-based ROP (Return-Oriented Programming) attack detection system that leverages microarchitecture-independent program characteristics. Unlike prior hardware performance counter-based approaches, EigenROP avoids masking underlying program behavior. The key insight is that ROP gadgets disrupt normal program execution patterns, creating detectable anomalies in relationships among program characteristics. The system achieves 81% detection accuracy with only 0.8% false positives, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art microarchitectural defenses (49-68% accuracy). EigenROP uses statistical learning to identify principal components in program snapshots, comparing real-time measurements against a learned baseline. The approach is robust against recent ROP evasion techniques like call-preceded gadgets and history-flushing attacks, as it doesn't rely on branch tracing or gadget length. While promising, EigenROP faces challenges with very short ROP chains and overhead reduction, suggesting future hardware support could further improve performance.
paper_title: EigenROP: Detecting ROP with Statistical Learning of Program Characteristics
